description: Replace the selected n1024 path s profiled 11.306 ms tridiagonal solve and reflector backtransform with a fused B200 device phase: co-schedule bisection or inverse iteration, rolling reorthogonalization, and compact-WY panel application using warp-specialized shared staging or tensor cores; retain the two-CTA reducer, two exact strict-tail corrections, hard-batch fallback, mapped classifier, certificates, CUDA guards, and every other size.

Replaced the n1024 40-tile near-max-SMEM scalar grouped solver with four 256-thread global-workspace tiles that fuse 25-step Sturm bisection and two inverse iterations, reusing the dead reduced matrix for factors. NVCC rejected the first launch spelling because band_eigh's runtime n cannot be a non-type template parameter; the structural implementation reached device compilation and needs the literal 1024 specialization.

Specialized the n1024 solve as four 256-thread tiles per matrix, fusing 25-step Sturm bisection and two inverse iterations while using the dead reduced matrix as coalesced global factor workspace instead of 40 near-max-SMEM 26-eigenpair tiles. All 39 validations pass. Full geomean improves 31499.025->31106.594 us and dense n1024 52601.568->44392.180 us; hard classifier routes remain 106015/105716/102776 us. Exact profile cuts the solve 11.306->3.117 ms; reducer remains 29.825 ms, rolling reorth 2.447 ms, compact-WY construction 1.346 ms.

Co-scheduled the four n1024 Sturm/inverse-iteration tiles as one four-CTA cluster per matrix, then kept the cluster resident to perform the exact rolling 16-column clustered reorthogonalization across all 1024 eigenvectors before exit. Removed 32 standalone reorth cluster launches. All 39 validations pass. Full metric improves 31106.594->31033.588 us; dense n1024 falls 44392.180->43054.581 us. Exact profile combines the prior 3.117 ms solve plus 2.447 ms reorth into one 4.390 ms kernel, saving 1.174 ms; reducer and tensor-core WY phases remain unchanged.

Replaced the eight serial 128-column compact-WY recurrences with the algebraically equivalent upper-triangular inverse T=(diag(1/tau)+triu(V^T V,1))^-1, using batched cuBLAS TRSM and retaining the existing tensor-core panel projections/applies. All 39 validations pass. Full metric is 31021.248 us versus 31033.588; dense n1024 falls 43054.581->42597.505 us. Exact profile replaces 1.346 ms of compact_wy_t kernels with 0.544 ms of batched TRSM plus 0.041 ms upper-triangle construction; fused solve/reorth remains 4.383 ms.

Reshaped the fused n1024 solve/reorth cluster from four 256-thread tiles to two 512-thread tiles, so the 60-matrix active batch launches 120 CTAs in one B200 SM wave while preserving 1024 cluster threads for identical rolling reorthogonalization. All 39 validations pass. Full metric is 30997.731 us versus 31021.248 and dense n1024 42531.361 versus 42597.505 us. Exact profile reduces the fused phase 4.383->4.252 ms; batched TRSM is 0.547 ms and all other routes remain intact.

Completed the fused launch sweep with one 1024-thread CTA per n1024 matrix, eliminating all inter-CTA DSM synchronization while retaining the same fused bisection, inverse iteration, and rolling reorthogonalization. All 39 validations pass, but dense n1024 rises 42531.361->43282.825 us and full metric to 31052.990. Exact profile measures the fused phase at 5.095 ms versus 4.252 ms for two 512-thread CTAs, so spreading each matrix across two CTAs is the selected geometry.

Restored the selected two-CTA fused solve and reassociated each n1024 compact-WY panel from V*(T*(V^T*Q)) to (V*T)*(V^T*Q), keeping all three products on B200 tensor cores while reducing the middle product's row extent. All 39 validations pass. Dense n1024 improves 42531.361->42444.022 us and full metric is 30992.266 us; the small gain brackets the reassociation near noise. Exact profile keeps solve/reorth at 4.249 ms and TRSM at 0.544 ms; WY CUTLASS families shift from 14/18/7 calls to 14/20/7 with similar aggregate time.

Doubled n1024 compact-WY panels from 128 to 256 columns, reducing the reverse reflector schedule from eight groups to four while retaining batched triangular construction and tensor-core application. All 39 validations pass. Dense n1024 improves 42444.022->42137.814 us, while unrelated sizes leave the full metric at 30997.717 us. Exact profile shows fused solve/reorth 4.275 ms, but cuBLAS TRSM grows 0.544->0.675 ms and still launches 16 kernels; wider CUTLASS families trade launch count for larger panel products.

Completed the compact-WY granularity sweep at 64 columns, expanding the reverse reflector schedule to 16 batched triangular/tensor-core groups while shrinking each T and V*T product. All 39 validations pass, but dense n1024 regresses from the 256-column point 42137.814->43832.644 us and full metric to 31057.713. The additional small-K tensor-core and TRSM launches outweigh reduced triangular work; 128 and 256 columns bracket the useful range.

Replaced the custom tensor-core compact-WY backtransform with one ATen ORMQR library operation over the stored n1024 Householder vectors and taus. The cuSOLVER-backed path is much more accurate (dense validation scaled eigen/orthogonality residuals 0.027/0.491 versus 8.75/8.49 for 64-column TF32 WY) and all 39 cases pass, but dense n1024 rises to 193808.192 us and full metric to 34829.763. The non-batched SIMT reflector application is over 4.5x slower than the custom B200 tensor-core route.

Restored the 256-column tensor-core WY path and moved exact certification before the unconditional full-batch Newton correction, relying on the retained two strict unsafe-tail corrections. All 39 tests pass, but dense n1024 rises 42137.814->61172.245 us and full metric to 31853.469. Exact profile shows 16 matrices remain unsafe after both strict corrections and enter cuSOLVER repair (4.704 ms n1024 sytrd plus 3.721 ms n512 stages and ~8 ms SIMT GEMMs), so the inexpensive full-batch high-precision correction is required to keep the active batch repair-free.

Replaced two shifted Thomas inverse iterations with one twisted LDL^T eigenvector construction: forward/backward factorizations select the minimum-residual twist, build both vector halves outward, and feed the same fused rolling reorthogonalizer. All 39 tests pass and the fused solve/reorth profile drops 4.275->3.311 ms, but 16 benchmark matrices remain certificate-unsafe and trigger cuSOLVER repair (4.750 ms n1024 sytrd plus 3.774 ms n512 stages); dense n1024 is 52978.208 us and full metric 31523.369. A refinement from the twisted seed is the measured next variant.

Refined each twisted n1024 eigenvector once by solving against its already-built unshifted LDL^T factors, adding forward/back substitution and normalization without a second factorization. All 39 tests pass. The fused phase rises 3.311->4.166 ms, yet the same 16 benchmark matrices still enter cuSOLVER repair (4.730 ms n1024 sytrd and 3.751 ms n512 stages); dense n1024 remains 52876.288 us and full metric 31532.425. Reusing the nearly singular unshifted factors does not change the certificate basin.

Changed the twisted-vector refinement from the nearly singular reused LDL^T to one freshly factorized lambda-2eps shifted system, then applied one Thomas solve before rolling reorthogonalization. All 39 validations pass, but dense n1024 remains 53292.120 us and full metric 31524.246, matching the repair-bearing twisted variants rather than the 42137.814 us two-pass baseline. A single negative-shift refinement does not recover the active benchmark certificate basin.

Switched the single twisted-vector refinement from lambda-2eps to the complementary lambda+2eps factorization used by the known passing solver's second pass. All 39 tests pass, but dense n1024 remains 53310.983 us and full metric 31553.535, so neither single shifted refinement reaches the no-repair basin from the twisted seed. The two-pass global solver remains the robust selected eigenvector path.

Compacted fused n1024 reorthogonalization into an ordered device list stored in the dead factor workspace: rank 0 scans eigenvalue gaps once, then the resident two-CTA cluster synchronizes and normalizes only listed columns instead of executing two cluster barriers for all 1024 columns. The original two-pass inverse solver and exact rolling 16-column corrections are unchanged. All 39 validations pass. Dense n1024 improves 42137.814->41326.294 us and full metric to 30927.398. Exact profile cuts fused solve/reorth 4.275->3.472 ms, an 0.803 ms reduction, with no cuSOLVER repair.

Combined compacted reorth with a hybrid reverse WY schedule: two 256-column panels on the short late tails and four 128-column panels on the tall early tails, reducing early V*T work while adding two tensor-core/TRSM groups. All 39 validations pass, but dense n1024 regresses 41326.294->41685.174 us and full metric to 30957.246. The launch/efficiency cost exceeds the saved early factor work; uniform 256-column groups remain selected.

Applied compact WY by solving M*X=V^T*Q directly for each uniform 256-column panel, eliminating explicit T, the identity RHS, and V*T before the final V*X update. All 39 validations pass and residuals improve, but the larger triangular RHS raises dense n1024 41326.294->42636.735 us and full metric to 31012.391. Batched TRSM throughput is lower than explicit-T construction plus tensor-core reassociation, which remains selected.

Moved clustered Rayleigh quotient recomputation into the resident n1024 solve/reorth cluster, preserving original eigenvalue gaps in dead factor workspace and eliminating the localized-value clone plus standalone Rayleigh kernel. All 39 validations pass. Dense n1024 is statistically unchanged at 41326.571 versus 41326.294 us and full metric is 30928.402 versus 30927.398 us. Exact profile measures the fused kernel at 3.552 ms versus 3.472 ms while removing the former ~0.107 ms standalone launch, leaving the net phase near noise; the fused form is retained for the next geometry sweep because it shortens the launch graph without changing repairs.

Retested the fused compact-list solve as four 256-thread CTAs per n1024 matrix, now that rank-0 compaction removes full-cluster barriers for unlisted columns. All 39 validations pass. Dense n1024 improves 41326.571->41304.309 us and full metric 30928.402->30924.149 us, both small relative to run variation. Exact profile measures the four-CTA fused phase at 3.479 ms versus 3.552 ms for two 512-thread CTAs, so four CTAs recover ~0.073 ms while preserving the same solve and repair behavior.

Completed the compact-list geometry sweep with one 1024-thread CTA per n1024 matrix, eliminating inter-CTA cluster exchange while retaining fused Rayleigh updates. All 39 validations pass, but dense n1024 regresses 41304.309->41936.192 us and full metric rises 30924.149->30970.046 us. Exact profile measures the one-CTA fused phase at 4.190 ms versus 3.479 ms for four 256-thread CTAs; reduced occupancy and per-CTA issue throughput dominate synchronization savings.

Extended the compact-list launch sweep to the maximum portable eight-CTA cluster, with 128 eigenpairs per CTA and the same 1024 cluster threads. All 39 validations pass. The sampled dense n1024 time improves 41304.309->41246.058 us and full metric reaches 30905.966 us, but unrelated sizes also moved favorably. Exact profile measures the fused phase at 3.490 ms versus 3.479 ms for four 256-thread CTAs, so the apparent end-to-end edge is benchmark noise; four CTAs remain the profile-selected geometry.

Restored the profile-selected four-CTA solver and completed the compact-WY width sweep with two 512-column reverse panels, halving high-level panel groups. All 39 validations pass, but dense n1024 regresses 41304.309->42382.710 us and full metric rises to 30997.715. Exact profile keeps fused solve at 3.484 ms, while batched triangular inversion grows from ~0.674 to 1.195 ms and wider factor products add enough cost that launch reduction cannot compensate; 256-column panels remain selected.

Restored 256-column WY and reduced n1024 Sturm bisection from 25 to 24 iterations, keeping two shifted inverse iterations and fused compact-list reorthogonalization. All 39 fixed validations pass, but the active dense batch rises 41304.309->53109.792 us and full metric to 31524.061. Exact profile saves only ~0.029 ms in the fused phase (3.455 versus 3.484 ms) while 16 matrices become certificate-unsafe and trigger 4.749 ms n1024 plus 3.771 ms n512 cuSOLVER sytrd repair; 25 iterations is the measured no-repair threshold.

Parameterized inverse-iteration count and tested one shifted Thomas pass on only the selected n1024 path, restoring 25-step bisection and 256-column WY. All 39 fixed tests pass via retained repair, but every active dense matrix becomes unsafe: dense n1024 rises 41304.309->163133.108 us and full metric to 34364.890. Exact profile cuts the fused kernel 3.484->2.319 ms, then full-batch cuSOLVER repair dominates with ~30 ms symv, ~16.8 ms gemvx, ~17.3 ms large SIMT GEMMs, and dense eigensolver stages. Two inverse iterations are required for the no-repair basin.

Factored one positive-shift n1024 tridiagonal once per eigenpair and applied the same LDL factors twice, preserving two inverse solves while eliminating the second factorization; specialization is confined to fused n1024. All 39 tests pass, but 16 active matrices require repair, dense n1024 is 52871.344 us, and full metric 31535.872. Exact profile unexpectedly raises the fused phase from 3.484 to 3.670 ms after splitting factor/solve loops, then adds 4.736 ms n1024 and 3.753 ms n512 sytrd repair. Complementary negative/positive factors remain both faster and necessary for certificates.

Restored the measured four-CTA, 25-step, complementary-shift solver with uniform 256-column compact-WY panels, then removed the now-unreachable standalone tiled reorthogonalization and Rayleigh kernels. The resulting tree differs from trial 19 only by 186 lines of dead-code deletion. Final build and all 39 validations pass. Final full metric is 30940.816 us (run-to-run variation versus trial 19's 30924.149), while the target dense n1024 shape improves 41304.309->41266.977 us. Exact final profile measures reducer 29.894 ms, fused solve/reorth/Rayleigh 3.482 ms, TRSM 0.674 ms, and no cuSOLVER repair.

Confirmed the maximum portable eight-CTA, 128-thread n1024 solve cluster on the cleaned selected tree. All 39 validations pass. The repeat dense n1024 result is 41253.952 us versus 41266.977 us for the immediately preceding four-CTA confirmation, and full metric is 30919.549 versus 30940.816; the earlier eight-CTA sample reached 41246.058 us and 30905.966. Exact final profile measures reducer 29.880 ms, fused solve/reorth/Rayleigh 3.483 ms, TRSM 0.674 ms, and no cuSOLVER repair. The clean selected commit removes 186 dead legacy kernel lines and retains every fallback, certificate, strict correction, CUDA guard, and non-n1024 route.

Selected clean commit cc8c30fbce6caa9f7e97bec0c2bde92bdf29741e after 28 logged trials. Against parent 31499.025 us, the final repeat is 30919.549 us; the selected eight-CTA geometry also sampled 30905.966 us earlier. Dense n1024 falls from the parent 52601.568 to 41253.952 us final, with an earlier 41246.058 us sample. All 39 tests pass, kernelguard is clean, and the exact final profile is brief-40-trial-27-cc8c30fbc.nsys-rep: reducer 29.880 ms, fused solve/reorth/Rayleigh 3.483 ms versus parent solve 11.306 plus reorth 2.448 ms, TRSM 0.674 ms, and no cuSOLVER repair. Main measured steps were global-workspace Sturm/inverse solve; resident clustered reorth; triangular-inverse compact WY; tensor-core reassociation; 64/128/256/512 and hybrid panel schedules; 1/2/4/8-CTA geometry; compacted cluster lists; fused Rayleigh updates; direct TRSM, ORMQR, twisted-vector/refinement, 24-step bisection, one-pass inverse, and factor reuse variants. Repair-bearing variants measured 52.9-163.1 ms dense and were not selected. The final cleanup removes 186 unreachable legacy kernel lines while retaining both strict corrections, classifier/fallbacks, certificates, guards, and every other size. Concrete openings remain: a custom SM100 triangular-inverse plus V*T kernel to replace 16 TRSM launches, TMA/shared staging for WY panels, warp-specialized Sturm scans that share recurrence work across nearby eigenvalues, and a persistent cluster schedule that overlaps factor workspace traffic with inverse iteration without weakening the complementary-shift certificate basin.
